user_stories.story: As the maintainer, I want the description rules (required, trimmed, 1 to 200 characters) declared on a Pydantic model instead of a hand-written function, so the rules live in one declarative place (checklist item 3).
As an API client, I want every response (status, plain-string detail, precedence) to stay exactly as it is today, so nothing observable changes.
As the maintainer, I want photo checks left hand-written, so the change stays small.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: models.py defines a Pydantic (v2) model for the description whose field uses min_length=1 and max_length=MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS (the existing constant, not a repeated literal 200) with whitespace trimming applied before the length checks. Pass: inspecting the model shows these constraints; the model is used by both POST and PUT.

routes.py no longer contains hand-written length/blank checks for the description (the body of _validate_description is replaced by model validation or the function is removed). Photo validation functions (_validate_files, _read_all, _detect_extensions, remove_photos checks) are unchanged in behavior.

The model is applied to the already-parsed form (value of form.get("description") inside the existing request.form() block), NOT as a FastAPI Form/dependency parameter on the handlers. Pass: handler signatures remain (request) / (log_id, request) and the 413-before-422 body limit and PUT 404-before-form ordering are unaffected.
Missing description, empty string, whitespace-only string, and a description sent as a file part each return 422 with detail exactly "description is required and cannot be blank" (POST and PUT).

A description longer than 200 characters after trimming returns 422 with detail exactly "description must be at most 200 characters" (POST and PUT). Exactly 200 after trimming is accepted. Length counts code points (200 emoji accepted, 201 rejected).
Accepted descriptions are stored and returned trimmed (leading/trailing whitespace removed, inner text unchanged).
Error bodies are always {"detail": ""}; FastAPI/Pydantic default list-of-errors bodies never appear for description errors.

Status precedence is unchanged: body over limit 413 > request-shape 422 (description checked before photo count/file shape/extension) > oversized photo 413 > content 422 > 500. PUT on an unknown id still returns 404 before any form/description validation. Existing precedence test (oversized photo + blank description gives 422) still passes.

All existing tests pass unchanged (no edits to or weakening of existing tests), including backend/tests/test_validation.py. Run with TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/dailylog_test and DATABASE_URL unset.

At least one new focused test (new test function, existing ones untouched) covers the model directly or an uncovered edge, e.g. non-string input mapping to the blank message, or whitespace-only combined with an over-limit photo.
No new dependencies; requirements files unchanged; no change to specs.md contract text beyond optionally none.

assumptions.assumption: Design decision (planner's call): validate the already-parsed form value with the Pydantic model rather than using FastAPI's Form-model parameter. Justification: a FastAPI Form dependency parses the body and validates before the handler runs, so it would (a) run before the PUT 404 existence check, (b) interleave with the app's 413 handling and the hand-ordered shape checks (description before photo count), and (c) emit FastAPI's default list-of-errors 422 body, which would need a global exception handler that also affects other routes (e.g. the non-integer id 422 would be unaffected only if carefully scoped). Validating inside the existing form block keeps all three contracts with the smallest change.

Pydantic ValidationError is translated in routes (or a small helper) to the two existing detail strings by error type: too-long gives the length message; everything else (missing, wrong type such as an UploadFile, too short after trimming) gives the blank message.
Pydantic's whitespace stripping is equivalent to str.strip() for the tested inputs (spaces, tabs, newlines).
Only description moves to Pydantic; remove_photos text check and photo checks stay as they are.

The generic 500 handling and except HTTPException passthrough in handlers stay; a ValidationError must be converted to HTTPException(422) before reaching the generic except so it is not turned into a 500.

edge_cases.case: description sent as a file part (UploadFile, not str).
200 characters with surrounding whitespace (accepted); 201 characters with surrounding whitespace (rejected); 201 emoji rejected, 200 emoji accepted.
Repeated description fields: behavior stays as today (form.get returns the last value).
Oversized photo plus blank description: 422 for description, not 413.
PUT unknown id with invalid description: 404.
Rejected PUT leaves database rows and files unchanged.

risks.risk: Mapping Pydantic error types to the two detail strings could misclassify a case (e.g. non-str input); covered by existing and new tests.

Pydantic strict/lax str handling could coerce non-str values (bytes, numbers) differently from the old isinstance check; form values are only str or UploadFile, so UploadFile must still map to the blank message.
Switching to a FastAPI Form parameter instead would silently change precedence and the error body; this spec forbids it.

spec.dependencies: pydantic v2 (already installed via fastapi==0.162.0); files: backend/models.py, backend/routes.py, backend/tests/test_validation.py (read-only for existing tests), backend/tests/conftest.py, specs.md (contract, unchanged).
spec.self_critique: Each user story maps to criteria: story 1 to 1-3, story 2 to 4-9, story 3 to 2. All criteria are observable via code inspection or tests. Biggest remaining risk: the exact Pydantic error-type mapping for odd inputs (UploadFile, missing key) and where in the handler the conversion to HTTPException sits relative to the generic except; the existing suite is the safety net.
